An endearment is anything — a word, a phrase, or an action — that expresses love, affection, or tenderness toward someone. When you use an endearment, you are showing that you care about someone deeply, that they are dear (precious, beloved) to you.

Think of it as a small, warm gesture — verbal or otherwise — that says: "You matter to me. I feel close to you."

1. As a specific word or phrase (a "term of endearment")

This is the most common use. A term of endearment is a special nickname or loving label you call someone to show affection. These are not their real names — they are words chosen because they feel warm and intimate.

Examples of terms of endearment:

  • "Darling," "sweetheart," "honey," "dear," "love," "baby," "my precious," "angel"

A parent calling their child "my little sunshine" — that's a term of endearment.
A husband calling his wife "darling" — that's a term of endearment.
A grandmother calling you "dear" — that's a term of endearment.

These words are not meant to be taken literally. You don't actually think the person is honey or an angel. The word is chosen because its feeling is soft, sweet, and loving.

2. As an act or gesture (something done to show affection)

Endearment can also refer to a behavior or gesture that shows tenderness. Here, it is more abstract — it refers to the quality of being affectionate.

  • A mother gently brushing her child's hair before school — that is an act of endearment.
  • A friend remembering your favorite snack and bringing it for you — that could be described as an endearment.

In this sense, you might hear sentences like:

  • "He won her trust through small endearments — little notes, thoughtful gestures, a gentle tone."
  • "She showed her love not through grand gestures but through quiet endearments."

Endearments are used between people who share closeness or warmth. This includes:

  • Romantic partners: A couple calling each other "baby" or "love."
  • Parents and children: A parent saying "come here, sweetheart."
  • Close friends: An older friend calling you "dear" in a tender moment.
  • Grandparents and grandchildren: Calling a grandchild "my precious."

In some cultures and regions, even strangers use terms of endearment as a general friendly habit. In parts of Britain, for example, a shopkeeper might call a customer "love" or "dear" — not because they know them, but because it is a culturally warm and informal way of speaking.

• Singular (endearment) — refers to the concept, the quality, or a single act/instance.
    • "He spoke to her with great endearment." (with warmth and affection)
    • "It was a simple act of endearment."
  • Plural (endearments) — refers to multiple loving words or phrases spoken to someone.
    • "She whispered endearments as she held the baby."
    • "He showered her with endearments every morning."
The most important phrase to know

"Term of endearment" is the single most common phrase built from this word. If you remember nothing else, remember this: a term of endearment is a loving nickname or affectionate word used to address someone you care about.

• It is not flattery. Flattery is saying nice things to get something. Endearment comes from genuine affection.
  • It is not a formal compliment. Telling someone "your work is excellent" is a compliment, not an endearment.
  • It is not a regular name or title. Calling someone by their actual name (John, Sarah) is not an endearment. The word has to carry warmth, affection, or intimacy to qualify.
Putting it all together — example sentences

1. "Darling" and "sweetheart" are common terms of endearment in English.
  2. He looked at his daughter with endearment, unable to hide how much he loved her.
  3. She whispered soft endearments to calm the frightened child.
  4. The old couple still exchanged endearments after fifty years of marriage.
  5. Calling someone "dear" can be an endearment, but it can also sound condescending depending on the tone.

If you want one image to anchor this word in your memory: picture a grandparent cupping a child's face in their hands and saying "my darling." That moment — the word spoken, the warmth felt, the love expressed — that is endearment in its purest form.
